rounds.text: SK Minerals & Additives Ltd is fundamentally under-appreciated because its strategic pivot toward manufacturing promises a lucrative structural transformation [E14]. Management is actively scaling its higher-margin polymer additives segment—targeting robust 40% margins compared to current manufacturing levels of approximately 30%—backed by a newly acquired 9.6-acre facility and a phased capacity expansion to 18,000 metric tons within 12 to 18 months [E19, E22]. This ambitious operational shift is underpinned by strong sector tailwinds in chemicals, where sector median sales growth sits at 15.3% and profit growth reaches an impressive 41.7% [E10, E11, E12]. Furthermore, the company commands a solid revenue foundation via a Rs. 55 crore order book, heavily anchored by Rs. 42 crores in stable government contracts [E23, E24]. Conceded: institutional holdings have declined significantly and near-term raw material inflation and teething problems have weighed on margins [E3, E21, E30]. However, with insider ownership remaining steady and high at 73.53%, promoters retain strong skin-in-the-game alignment to execute on their vision of driving manufacturing contribution up to 50% of total revenue [E1, E14].
